inputs.content: The CEO was not available to answer questions; the team chose and recorded these: (1) deep deck (client diagnostic), navy theme, work only from the briefing pack; (2) FY2026 is treated as the first plan year and the covenant year, as the pack does; (3) promotional share target: the FY2024 level of 26.2%; (4) net labor-hour cut of 4%, taken in the Q3–Q4 stores; (5) shrink target: Q1–Q2 stores to the Q3 rate; (6) private label grows at its FY2025 pace (0.8 pp a year) for three years; (7) no sales growth to FY2028; (8) all nine weak stores closed in the base case, three after a board vote; (9) the same $96 basket for delivered and click-and-collect orders.

problem.statement: How can Harlow lift operating margin from 1.0% to at least 3.0% by FY2028, within $25M of one-time cost and the FY2026 covenant, and what comes first?
problem.decision_maker: CEO, presenting the margin plan for board approval
success_criteria: Operating margin of at least 3.0% by FY2028
At most $25M of one-time cost or capital over FY2026–FY2028
Operating income of at least $20M in FY2026 (lender covenant)
No closure of a store with a lease beyond 2027 without a board vote; delivery kept in some form
problem.accuracy: Order of magnitude (±20% on each move); briefing pack only, no outside data
out_of_scope: Broad price increases and new stores

one_day_answer.situation: Sales grew 6% from FY2023 to FY2025, but operating margin fell from 3.4% to 1.0%
one_day_answer.complication: Management blames wages and plans an 8% hours cut, yet promotions, shrink and home delivery explain most of the fall, and the cut risks more shrink
one_day_answer.resolution: Cut money-losing promotions, reprice delivery, rebalance labor toward fresh and receiving, and exit loss-making stores: about 3.2% by FY2028
